meta.description: Corrects the gene-independent copy-number artifact in CRISPR-Cas9 screens (Aguirre 2016 / Munoz 2016) where amplified loci appear essential from DNA-damage burden of simultaneous cuts. Covers CRISPRcleanR, CERES, Chronos (now with an accurate negative_control_sgrnas failure signature), the decision tree, and detect_cn_bias (now with a documented low-power floor and a no-cry-wolf guard on genuinely corrected screens).

scientific_integrity.detail: Every number in this audit came from a real program run: Chronos 2.3.15 (real HAP1 single-line data) or real/relabeled-real HT-29 gene-level LFC+CN data already on disk from the round-2 audit (CRISPRcleanR 3.0.1's own output). Relabeling exercises (Inputs 3, 4, 6) are explicitly disclosed as such, not presented as new wet-lab findings.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 7 independently confirms the round-2 Scope paragraph ('does not support treatment, therapy or other clinical recommendations... Decline the clinical part') is still present, byte-identical in intent, at the new commit.

methodological_ground.detail: Decision tree and thresholds remain grounded and correct (unchanged by this diff, previously verified). The new Reconciliation cause 5 is directionally sound (alternate_CN really does leave real residual signal, Input 5) even though its specific pooling-vs-per-line contrast did not reproduce -- an overclaim in illustration, not a methodological fallacy.

code_usability.detail: All tested code paths run as literally written: chronos.Chronos(...) construction with and without negative_control_sgrnas (Input 1), with an explicit empty dict (Input 6), and the full detect_cn_bias() function including its new low_power_n parameter and two new output fields at three different real/relabeled datasets and an exact boundary sweep (Inputs 2-5). No crashes, no syntax errors.

functional_suitability.note: Both round-3 targets (negative_control_sgrnas exception, detect_cn_bias low-power floor) are verified correct by real execution (Inputs 1-2). Docked 1 point: negative_control_sgrnas passed as an explicit empty dict {'screen': []} (rather than omitted) raises a different, undocumented ValueError ('set of negative_control_sgrnas is empty') that the Common Errors table does not cover (Input 6).

reliability.note: The Common Errors table's negative_control_sgrnas row now matches real behavior exactly, confirmed by independent execution, not a re-read of the fix log. Docked 1 point: the new Reconciliation cause 5's specific claim that pooling masks a per-line problem was not reproduced -- a real per-line-vs-pooled construction on real gene-effect data flagged the same bias both ways (Input 5).

performance_context.note: Unchanged from both prior audits: concise SKILL.md (~375 lines), separate usage-guide.md, one example file.

agent_usability.note: Both round-3 code paths (negative_control_sgrnas exception, low-power floor/suspicious_despite_ns) now run cleanly as documented on the first try (Inputs 1-4). Docked 1 point for the same Reconciliation overclaim affecting decision-guidance precision (Input 5).

human_usability.note: The negative_control_sgrnas exception documentation (type and call site) is now fully accurate on independent real execution, closing the round-2 Forgiveness gap; no new Forgiveness-category gap found by this audit's inputs.

security.note: Unchanged: no credentials, no injection vectors, no sensitive-data handling in any tested code path.

maintainability.note: Unchanged: no fixture/test data ships with the Skill, so documentation-vs-real-behavior drift can recur silently between audits -- which is exactly what this audit's own new inputs (5, 6) found again, independent of what the fixer was told to check.

agent_specific.note: The low-power floor gap is closed and independently confirmed both non-crying-wolf on a genuinely corrected screen (0/5 false alarms, Input 3) and boundary-correct at low_power_n=8 with no off-by-one error (Input 4). Docked 1 point: Chronos training still has no documented seed/determinism guidance (Idempotency), unchanged from both prior audits and unrelated to this fix pass.

key_strengths: Both round-3 targeted fixes are independently re-verified by fresh execution, not a re-read of the fix log: chronos.Chronos(...) construction raises the exact documented ValueError before train() is ever called (Input 1), and detect_cn_bias's low_power_floor/suspicious_despite_ns reproduce SKILL.md's documented real HT-29 numbers exactly (Input 2).

The 'no cry-wolf' claim this audit was explicitly asked to check is confirmed with real data: 0/5 false alarms when a genuinely diploid-LFC 'corrected' amplicon is tested, and the low_power_n=8 boundary plus the NaN guard are both off-by-one-free (Inputs 3-4).

recommendations.title: negative_control_sgrnas empty-dict case raises an undocumented ValueError
recommendations.problem: Passing negative_control_sgrnas as an explicit empty dict ({'screen': []}) rather than omitting the argument raises ValueError('set of negative_control_sgrnas is empty') -- a different message from the one the Common Errors table documents for the omitted-argument case.
recommendations.root_cause: The round-3 fix documented only the omitted-argument path, which was this audit's and the fix log's main test case; the empty-list path was mentioned only as an aside in the fix log and never added to SKILL.md itself.
recommendations.fix: Add a second Common Errors row: 'ValueError: set of negative_control_sgrnas is empty' at Chronos(...) construction | negative_control_sgrnas supplied but its list is empty | Populate it with real non-targeting/non-essential sgRNAs, not an empty list.

recommendations.title: Reconciliation cause 5's 'pooling masks it' claim did not reproduce on real per-line-vs-pooled data
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's new cause 5 justifies re-running detect_cn_bias per cell line by claiming pooling can mask a real per-line problem. A real construction from the round-2 fix pass's own 3-line panel found pooled and per-line gave the same qualitative read (both bias_present=True, near-identical gap) -- the specific masking scenario was not demonstrated.
recommendations.root_cause: The cause-5 text was added as prose reasoning during the fix pass and was never itself run against real numbers before this audit.
recommendations.fix: Soften the claim to what is actually demonstrated: alternate_CN's fitted average can leave real residual signal at strong amplicons (confirmed), and re-checking per line is good practice regardless of whether pooling happens to mask it in a given panel -- drop the implication that pooling reliably hides the problem.

recommendations.title: Chronos training has no documented seed/determinism guidance
recommendations.problem: None of the three real Chronos training runs across this audit's inputs set or discussed a random seed, and SKILL.md gives no guidance on reproducibility between training runs.
recommendations.root_cause: Carried over from both prior audits' static notes (Idempotency, Agent-Specific); unrelated to and untouched by this fix pass.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line note to the Chronos code block: set a seed (or document that Chronos training is stochastic and gene-effect estimates should be treated as approximate across runs) so agents don't present a single run's numbers as exactly reproducible.
